newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes firm on FOMC decision.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes firm on FOMC decision.

text.p: The Mexican peso reversed early weakness to close sharply stronger against the dollar on Tuesday after the Federal Open market Committee decided not to change U.S. interest rate policy, traders said.
"The FOMC decision enhanced confidence, even though it had been largely discounted," a dealer said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart closed 2.7 and 3.2 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.8550/7.8600 and 7.8490/7.8540 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts closed earlier 0.1 of a centavo weaker at 7.8650/7.8700 per dollar.
"The FOMC news came just (15 minutes) before the close, so we won't see its full impact on the foreign exchange market until tomorrow," another trader said.
Traders said the peso was also strong due to long dollar positions still being sold on the market and foreign investors switching to peso investments.
Dealers situated strong resistance for the 48-hour peso at 7.8550 per dollar.
Dealers said the peso's performance on Wednesday would also depend on the primary Cetes auction, whose results were due late Tuesday.

A Reuters survey of 11 money market traders showed they expected bellwether 28-day Cetes to be assigned at an average rate of 28.23 percent, which would be 94 basis points above last week's auction rate.
